notes: How hard each dangerous operation is to authorize. Read by the shared confirmation gate; it is deliberately NOT the chat clearance file. telegram_support_commands.json says WHO may ask for an operation, this says HOW HARD it is to confirm once asked, and the shared layer reads no chat settings at all - which is what lets the same confirmation apply to a shell caller, a scheduled run and a chat message. An operation missing from this file is confirmed at the STRICTEST level, not the weakest: two answers, the second one the target's own id typed out.

100.note: Takes a machine or a service down. Two answers: 'yes', then the target's own id typed out. The second answer cannot be given from muscle memory - it has to be read off the prompt - and a payload written for one host is rejected by another.

50.note: No downtime, but a large blast radius: rolls back a transaction, moves a file, starts work on a production instance. One typed 'yes'.
